_note: Eight questions, drawn per §18.3 from things that actually confused somebody working on
this project — not from any bundle's table of contents, which flatters the bundle by
construction. Provenance is recorded per question in `from`, so a reader can check the
set was not reverse-engineered from the answers.
Every `answerable_from` file is in the CONTROL arm, which `run.py --check` enforces: the
bundle is a shortcut to knowledge that exists either way, never the only copy. A question
answerable only inside the bundle measures whether a file was deleted.
`claims` is what a correct answer contains, graded blind. Omitting one is a gap; stating
something false is a defect and gets traced back to whichever concept caused it.

questions.from: asked verbatim while configuring this repository: 'i excluded decisions then reran and it still shows'
questions.text: I added a folder to `build.exclude` and re-ran the build, but that folder's concepts still show up in the web UI. What did I misunderstand, and what do I actually have to change?
claims: `exclude` controls what the build READS; `bundles` controls what the mesh IS
the build stops mirroring the folder, but a `bundles` entry still names it, so every reader still finds it by path
the fix is to remove the `bundles.<id>` line, not to add another exclude
keeping both is correct when the folder is an in-place bundle the build must not mirror

questions.from: the rule the enrichment loop is built around, and the one a new contributor reliably proposes removing
questions.text: The build already knows a source file changed. Why doesn't it just refresh that concept's `okfm_captured` for me?
claims: refreshing it automatically would erase the very signal drift exists to carry
clearing drift is a human act — it asserts somebody reviewed the concept against its source
`revalidate` rejects a `process:` actor and requires `human:`
drift is observed at build time and cached; nothing resolves it at read time

questions.from: the design choice a two-state boolean would have got wrong, and did in an earlier draft
questions.text: A concept points at a source that has never been observed. Does a reader treat that pointer as fresh or as drifted?
claims: neither — there is a third state, `unknown`
the three states are match, drifted, and unknown
defaulting an unobserved pointer to fresh would be a stored opinion wearing a computed one's clothes
the cache stores observations, not verdicts, which is why caching it does not violate derive-don't-store

questions.from: asked while adding the Ollama path: if it costs nothing and needs no key, why isn't it level 2?
questions.text: Drafting with a model on my own machine costs no money and needs no API key. Why is that component still not allowed to sit at level 2?
claims: the level 2 / level 3 boundary is exactly the `model` line
it is mechanically checked — `dev/check_levels.py` admits nothing beyond `human` at level 2
it is named Level 2+ for what it costs an adopter, which is a name and not a relocation
the component still declares `needs-model` and still sits in the level 3 bundle

questions.from: done for real when the decision records left the mesh; three things were left behind
questions.text: I want to stop publishing one of my bundles. What do I change, and what gets left behind that I have to clean up myself?
claims: remove that bundle's entry from `bundles` in the config
the build deletes member concepts it wrote itself, in the mesh's own `members/` folder
a member concept the build did not write is reported and left alone rather than deleted
the config check reports the bundle folder still sitting in the output directory

questions.from: the standing objection to the ownership table — extraction fills titles and descriptions, so why not edges
questions.text: The tooling extracts titles and descriptions without a model. Why won't it also infer `okfm_relations` from the markdown links already in the prose?
claims: traversal, impact analysis and drift propagation all read an edge as fact
a wrong typed edge is worse than a missing one
relations require a human; a model-tier component may propose them but not write them
an unknown predicate is rejected outright, unlike an unknown type which only warns

questions.from: the first question anyone asks before pasting the folder into their own repository
questions.text: What runtime does the deterministic build require, and what has to be installed before it will run?
claims: Python 3.13
standard library only — no third-party packages
no install step; the folder is copied and run

questions.from: a real design note in the pipeline, written after chasing the second failure instead of the first
questions.text: The build stops at the first failing step instead of running the remaining ones. Why was it built that way?
claims: a later step would read what the failed step did not write
that produces a second, misleading failure
the misleading one is the failure people chase
